subject: Reserved pool follow-up — GPU selection, TPS targets & concurrency action list
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@olive-sys.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + action items from today's sizing call

Hi Emily — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the concrete asks so we can move to a sizing proposal for Reserved (dedicated) capacity: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Target steady-state TPS: ~100–140 inference requests/sec (you mentioned 120 as the expected median with 95th at ~220).
- Typical token shape: median request prompt ~160 tokens, median model output ~900 tokens (long summaries + few-shot context).
- Latency SLO target: 95th <= 300ms for short responses, but you prioritized consistent tail for user-facing features.
- Preference: Dedicated reserved pool for predictable costs and data isolation; possible Private/VPC later for regulated customers. Hosted API is being kept as fallback for burst.

Concrete asks (owners in parentheses):
1) Confirm whether 120 TPS is the expected steady median or a growth target (Emily) — we used steady-state for sizing.
2) Provide 72-hour traffic sample (timestamps + token counts) or representative logs — needed to model batching and KV cache benefits (Emily / Prod Eng).
3) Decide on concurrency headroom (suggest +40% above median) — Redwood recommends starting with 1.4x concurrency envelope to hit tail SLOs (Karthik/Vanessa).
4) Review attached sizing workbook (olive_reserved_pool_proposal_v1.xlsx) with GPU flavor options and cost run rates; highlight any org constraints (procurement).

Immediate next steps:
- I'll iterate the workbook with two SKU options: A100/80GB (higher throughput, fewer nodes) vs H100/80GB (better fp16 perf and quantization path). Expect v2 by Tue EOD.
- Vanessa will sketch an ops runbook for failover to Hosted API for bursts.
- Mina will prepare a short compliance checklist for Private/VPC when you want to evaluate it.

Can you confirm the 120 TPS assumption and share the traffic sample by EOD Monday? If that's tight, tell us the earliest you can share.

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0190

Attachments: olive_reserved_pool_proposal_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), deployment_mode_tradeoff_onepager.pdf (pdf)
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@olive-sys.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Olive Systems Procurement <procurement@olive-sys.com>
Date: 2027-08-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + action items from today's sizing call

Thanks Karthik — good summary. A few quick clarifications: 

- 120 TPS is our target median for the first phase (Q4 soft launch). We expect peak day spikes of up to ~230 TPS for short windows (campaigns).
- We'll pull a 72-hour sample; engineering asked for until Friday AM to scrub PII. Expect a CSV with timestamp, request_tokens, response_tokens.
- Regarding GPUs, procurement has an internal preference for H100-class due to model types (longer sequence attention sparsity). But cost is a concern; please show the node counts and cost delta in the workbook.

We've looped procurement and I've copied them to help with cost/contract timeline. If your workbook has an ops mode that can fall back to Hosted for ephemeral 10–15 minute spikes, that would be ideal.

Emily
Principal Product Manager
Olive Systems
emily.zhao@olive-sys.com

Onboarding contact: procurement@olive-sys.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@olive-sys.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-08-15T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + action items from today's sizing call

Appreciate the confirmation, Emily — that helps. A couple follow-ups after internal sizing run: 

- With median=120 TPS and token mix median prompt=160 / output=900, our modeling shows two reasonable pools: 
  Option 1 (cost-optimized): 8x A100-80GB nodes (steady med throughput) + autoscale lanes for 2x burst; estimated committed monthly $X (see workbook).
  Option 2 (performance-priority): 6x H100-80GB nodes with slightly higher per-node throughput and lower latency for long outputs; estimated committed monthly $Y.

- Important nuance: if you use long-context attention patterns heavily, H100 shows 12–18% better token/sec for the ensemble of models you demoed. We can surface microbenchmarks.

- For tail SLOs we recommend concurrency headroom = 1.4x median (120 -> plan for 168 concurrent in-flight requests) and a KV/prefix cache policy to reduce repeated prompt costs (we'll validate once we have logs).

I'll attach a short microbenchmark summary in v2 and flag the per-token cost deltas. Vanessa — can you drop the initial failover playbook by EOD so procurement sees operational controls?

Thanks, Karthik
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@olive-sys.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Olive Systems Procurement <procurement@olive-sys.com>
Date: 2027-08-15T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + action items from today's sizing call

Emily / team — attaching a short ops sketch in the drive link (see thread metadata). Key points: 
- Failover plan: route bursts >180 TPS to hosted API lane with throttling policy; tokens continue billed to reserved pool at negotiated commit up to a fixed burst cap.
- Monitoring: 95th latency alerts, queue depth, GPU utilization dashboards.
- Rollout: canary on 10% traffic, 50% stage, cutover.

Notes for procurement: We can include an SLO addendum to guarantee reserved capacity availability and a credit policy for extended downtime. Happy to sync with procurement to outline SLA language.

- Vanessa
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@olive-sys.com>
Date: 2027-08-16T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + action items from today's sizing call

Emily — quick compliance note as you evaluate Private/VPC later: 
- Private/VPC adds network egress constraints and may require an HSM/KMS exchange flow. That typically adds 2–4 weeks to prep on our side for audited accounts.
- For your regulated customers, we can map required controls and generate an evidence packet (SOC2 sections + audit logs) once you confirm the list of customers who need private hosting.

I'll prepare the checklist and stub the DocuSign NDA for the packaging work if you want us to start.

Regards, Mina
Senior Security & Compliance Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@olive-sys.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, Olive Systems Procurement <procurement@olive-sys.com>
Date: 2027-08-16T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Next steps & timeline — sizing v2 ETA + procurement sync

Team — closing the loop on owners and ETA: 
- Karthik: deliver sizing workbook v2 (A100 vs H100 node counts + monthly cost estimates + microbenchmarks) — ETA: 2027-08-17T17:00-07:00.
- Vanessa: ops failover playbook + monitoring checklist — ETA: 2027-08-17T12:00-07:00.
- Mina: compliance checklist + preliminary DocuSign NDA for private/VPC evaluation — ETA: 2027-08-18T12:00-07:00.

Emily / Procurement — can we schedule a 30-min procurement-specific call next week to walk the cost delta and SCC? I'll send a calendar invite after I post v2. If the 72-hour sample lands before we finish v2, we'll rerun the model for more accurate batching gains.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to a pilot.

Karthik
